groups.title: Content Collections
groups.question: Your blog posts are Markdown files, and a missing date in one post broke the live site. Explain how content collections prevent this.

followUps.Collection Schema Definition: How does a collection schema catch bad frontmatter?
followUps.getCollection and getEntry APIs: What do getCollection and getEntry return?

evidence.text: A Zod schema defines the expected frontmatter fields.
Every entry is validated at build time.
Missing or wrong fields fail the build instead of breaking the live site.
getCollection returns all validated entries in a collection.
getEntry returns one entry by its id or slug.
Both are fully typed from the schema.

groups.title: MDX Integration
groups.question: Your editors want interactive charts inside posts and automatic syntax highlighting and table of contents. Explain MDX and remark and rehype plugins.

followUps.MDX Components and Slots: What does MDX add to Markdown?
followUps.Remark and Rehype Plugins: What is the difference between remark and rehype plugins?

evidence.text: MDX lets you import and use components inside Markdown.
It needs the MDX integration to be installed.
Editors can mix prose with interactive elements.

notEnough: Only saying MDX is Markdown with JSX.

evidence.text: Remark plugins work on the Markdown structure.
Rehype plugins work on the HTML produced from it.
They add things like syntax highlighting and table of contents.

groups.title: Frontmatter and Data Modeling
groups.question: Each post has an author, and author details are repeated and inconsistent across posts. Explain how you would model the content.

followUps.Typed Frontmatter with Zod: How do Zod types map to frontmatter fields?
followUps.Reference Fields Between Collections: How does reference() link posts to authors?

evidence.text: Schema types like string, date and array match the frontmatter values.
Dates in frontmatter can be parsed into real date objects.
Every entry is guaranteed to have the right shape.
reference() makes a field point to an entry in another collection.
The link is type-checked at build time.
Author details live in one place and posts only point to them.

notEnough: Only saying you can reference collections.

groups.title: Content Rendering
groups.question: You are rendering blog posts from your collection and building their URLs. Explain how the body is rendered and how slugs work.

followUps.render() and <Content /> Component: How do you render a post's Markdown body?
followUps.Slug Generation and URL Mapping: How are slugs generated and used for URLs?

evidence.text: Rendering an entry returns a Content component.
The Content component outputs the compiled HTML of the body.
Inserting the raw body string would skip the Markdown processing.

notEnough: Only saying you render the post.

evidence.text: Slugs or ids come from file names by default.
A custom slug field can override that.
getStaticPaths uses them to build each post's URL.
